bilingual.notes: Two standard routes: a Bilingual Education multi-age standalone license, or a Bilingual Education endorsement on a primary teaching license. Both require completion of an approved teacher-preparation program. No OAE content exam currently exists for Bilingual Education. A Bilingual Education supplemental license (no exam, no approved program) is available for up to 3 years as a bridge to the standard route.

eld.notes: Two standard routes: a TESOL multi-age standalone license, or a TESOL endorsement on a primary teaching license. Both require an approved teacher-preparation program and the Ohio Assessments for Educators (OAE) TESOL content exam. A Supplemental TESOL license is also available (test only, no approved program), valid for 1 year and renewable up to 3 years total.

history.title: Seal of Biliteracy authorized by Substitute SB 3
history.description: Ohio General Assembly enacted Substitute Senate Bill 3 (131st GA, 2016) authorizing a State Seal of Biliteracy. Program launched in the 2017–18 academic year for the Class of 2018 graduates; sealofbiliteracy.org records adoption as 2017-03-16.

history.title: EPAA 29(100) document analysis (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021)
history.description: Leider, Colombo & Nerlino published in Education Policy Analysis Archives 29(100) a comprehensive document analysis of every state and DC's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI teacher-credentialing requirements, professional teaching standards mentions, and EL-percentage figures, based on primary SEA sources collected October–December 2019. The 2019 coding of Ohio's EL-credentialing landscape is preserved as a temporally-anchored research baseline against which the catalog's later verifications are framed.

history.title: ODE renamed Ohio Department of Education and Workforce (ODEW)
history.description: House Bill 33 (FY24-25 biennial budget, signed 2023-07-04) reorganized and renamed the Ohio Department of Education to the Ohio Department of Education and Workforce. The education.ohio.gov domain continues to resolve and current SEA pages display the ODEW banner. Structural change only; EL-related teacher credentialing requirements were not altered.

history.title: ODE reorganized as Department of Education and Workforce (HB 33)
history.description: Ohio's biennial budget bill HB 33 (135th General Assembly, signed 2023-07-04) reorganized the Department of Education into the Department of Education and Workforce (ODEW), consolidating workforce-development functions under the new agency. The change was structural; EL credentialing rules under OAC 3301 carried over.

elPercentHistory.note: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce, October fall snapshot (77,152 EL students of 1,665,521 enrolled). Identification under O.R.C. 3301.0731 / federal ESEA definition: Language Usage Survey, OELPS screener, parent notification. The 0.8 percentage-point increase from NCES's fall 2021 value (3.8%) is a modest upward continuation of the NCES trajectory. Ohio does not publish a multi-year EL percentage table for fall 2018-2021 in directly accessible form, so methodological continuity with the prior NCES series cannot be confirmed from overlapping observations.
